questions.question: After installing the typescript npm package, what actually runs when I type tsc — is the compiler JavaScript?
questions.answerNote: No: bin/tsc imports lib/tsc.js, which resolves a native executable with getExePath() and replaces the Node process with it (process.execve on newer Node, otherwise execFileSync with stdio inherited, propagating the exit code). getExePath looks for the per-platform package @typescript/typescript-<platform>-<arch> (or built/local when run from the repo) and its lib/tsc binary; the compiler itself is the Go program under tsc/.

questions.question: If the compiler is a native binary, how does a Node program ask it questions like 'what is the type of this node'?
questions.answerNote: The TS API client spawns the native executable in API mode (tsc --api ...) and talks to it over stdio (or a named pipe/socket): the sync client uses a MessagePack RPC channel, the async client JSON-RPC (--async). Optional --callbacks let the Go side call back into JS for a virtual filesystem. On the Go side api.go parses the flags and starts the stdio server; session.go dispatches methods (initialize, snapshots, batched requests, etc.).

questions.question: Where is the logic that decides whether a value of one type can be assigned to a variable of another type?
questions.answerNote: In the Go checker: tsc/internal/checker/relater.go. isTypeAssignableTo calls isTypeRelatedTo(source, target, c.assignableRelation); the same machinery handles subtype, strict-subtype and comparable relations, with fresh literal types regularized first and structural comparison done by the relater.

questions.question: Does the compiler type-check files in parallel, and how does it decide which files share a checker?
questions.answerNote: Yes: the program owns a pool of several checkers, each with its own symbol/type caches and a mutex so it is used exclusively. Files are assigned to checkers by treating it as balanced graph partitioning over resolved imports, using a weighted streaming FENNEL heuristic (affinity to already-assigned importers minus a load penalty, with empirically tuned constants and a deliberate stream order) so related files share caches without lengthening the parallel critical path.

questions.question: When a project config inherits from another via 'extends', where is that merged, and where is the full list of allowed options declared?
questions.answerNote: tsconfigparsing.go (ParseJsonSourceFileConfigFileContent / parseConfig / getExtendsConfigPath...) resolves the extends chain (paths or package names, arrays allowed) and merges base options before the child's. Every option's name, short name, kind, category, description and default is a CommandLineOption entry in OptionsDeclarations in declscompiler.go (build/watch/typeAcquisition options in sibling decls*.go files).

questions.question: I changed compiler behaviour and a lot of expected-output test files now differ. How do I review and accept the new outputs?
questions.answerNote: Run npx hereby test (clears stale output and writes new results to tsc/testdata/baselines/local), diff local against tsc/testdata/baselines/reference, then npx hereby baseline-accept, which copies local into reference and deletes files marked .delete. Only accept right after a fresh hereby test run. Tasks are defined in Herebyfile.mjs.

questions.question: What are the thousands of tests in the fourslash folder testing, and how is one written?
questions.answerNote: Fourslash tests exercise editor/language-service features (completions, hover/quick info, go-to-definition, references, rename, code fixes, formatting) through the LSP server. Each is a Go test in fourslash/tests that embeds TypeScript source containing /*marker*/ positions, [|ranges|] and // @Filename: sections; test_parser.go parses that, NewFourslash spins up an in-memory LSP session, and the test calls f.GoToMarker/Insert/Verify* helpers, many of which write baselines.

questions.question: How does the editor language server start up, and where does an incoming request like 'go to definition' get routed?
questions.answerNote: main.go switches on --lsp and calls runLSP (lsp.go), which only supports --stdio and builds lsp.NewServer with stdin/stdout. Server.Run starts read, dispatch and write loops; handleRequestOrNotification looks the method up in a handler table populated with registerRequestHandler (e.g. TextDocumentDefinition, Completion, Rename) and runs it against the project session.

c4Note.note: At the pin the repo is the native (Go) TypeScript compiler: ~900 non-test Go files in tsc/ (checker, parser, binder, emitter, lsp, api, project system) plus npm packages that wrap it. The scan (prepared tree without tsc/testdata) sees only TS/JS, so it produced one container '@typescript/repo' from the root package.json with 158 components: packages/typescript's API client and generated enum files, the VS Code extension, tools/scripts and a few .mts generator scripts inside tsc/. The npm workspaces (packages/*) were collapsed into that single container, and the actual compiler is entirely invisible.
expectedContainers: native compiler CLI (tsc/cmd/tsc: tsc, --lsp, --api entry points)
language server + project system (tsc/internal/lsp, ls, project)
typescript npm package (packages/typescript: launcher + TS API client)
problems: Go is not extracted, so the entire compiler (tsc/internal/*, tsc/cmd) has no components; answers to most questions live there
npm workspaces packages/* collapsed into one root container '@typescript/repo' (sourceRef package.json)
packages/typescript/lib/tsc.js and getExePath.js (the npm launcher) skipped as '.js in a TypeScript repo' while lib/version.cjs and Herebyfile.mjs are included — inconsistent JS handling
the only tsc/ components are four codegen .mts scripts (tsc/internal/lsp/lsproto/_generate, stringutil/_scripts), which misrepresent tsc/ as tooling
dozens of generated enum files (packages/typescript/src/enums/*.enum.ts and *.ts) shown as individual architecture components
as-is scan fails with git ENOBUFS (all blobs read into a 128 MB buffer); only the prepared tree without tsc/testdata scans
